== Biography ==
{{Ireland Native}}
Hugh was a native of Ireland, the son of [[Glasgow-2539|John Glasgow]] of Gortin, Derryloran, County Tyrone;
<ref name="b"/>
and the uncle of [[Glasgow-2538|Thomas McNeice Glasgow]], a mine manager of Thames, New Zealand.
<ref>See Thomas's profile for citation of this.</ref>

Perhaps around the early 1830s, he moved to St. John, New Brunswick, or perhaps Nova Scotia -- his eldest son Hugh Adam was born at St. John in about 1835.

He passed away 30 November 1899 age 94, due to old age, and was buried at Cedar Hill Cemetery.
<ref name="b">{{Ancestry Tree Media|118447274|90edf6a6-f606-45dc-9fea-bf4bdaca22c1}} Burial request form -- uploaded to ancestry-com tree with no source attribution:
* Hugh Glasgow d. 30 Nov 1899 age 94 yrs, white male, widower.
* Lived on Hotiction(sp? Street, St. John N.B. Brooks Ward.
* Born Ireland
* Occupation: Crader (?)
* Father: John Glasgow.
* Interment: Cedar Hill Cemetery.
* COD: Old Age.
</ref>

He was one of the oldest residents of Carleton, and had lived there for over 60 years. He left three sons: H. Adams (superintendent of Carleton ferry), Edwin, and Albert who was in business in Denver, CO; and two daughters Mrs M. Turner and Mrs. Anthony Atchison.
<ref>[https://paperspast.natlib.govt.nz/newspapers/THS19000123.2.10?query=%22hugh+glasgow%22 ''(untitled)''], ''Thames Star'', Volume XXXIX, Issue 9554, 23 January 1900, Page 2; citing Wolfville, Nova Scotia newspaper.</ref>

Some ancestry-com trees have a Hugh Glasgow d. 1900 age 65 at Carleton, as father of Margaret wife of Alonzo Calder. This would be at odds with the newspaper notice, so perhaps those profile have made mistakes.

=== Passenger list ===
There is a passenger list of the ''Amethyst'' arriving in Boston in 1843 from St. George, New Brunswick, carrying a group of four Glasgows: Francis (36), Hugh (35), Mary (19), and Ellen (18). They were said to be emigrating to the U.S. This could well be the same family?

His daughters Margaret and H. Adam both give New Brunswick as their birthplace on censuses, although perhaps we should not rule out that they were born in Ireland prior to emigration.

=== Wives and children ===
Elizabeth Black was given as the mother on his children Ada and Edwin's death registrations.  But based on her age, she probably was not the mother of H. Adam and Margaret .

He could possibly be the father of [[Glasgow-1180|Sarah (Glasgow) Kermode (abt.1826-1894)]] too ? Sarah Kermode named her parents as Hugh and Margaret, and appears to be from Gortin, Derryloran.

There are some confirmations of Glasgow children of Gortin in the Derryloran parish register, including William (b. abt. 1822), Sally (abt. 1827) and Margaret (abt. 1830). These may or may not be Hugh's children; see [[Glasgow-2539|John Glasgow (bef.1771-)]] research notes for more detail.
